_meta.title: Theta / slow-gamma band edges - locked, cited inputs for the dimensionless gamma/theta ratio (neuro §03)
_meta.what: The two band edges that let the WORKING-MEMORY span ratio gamma/theta be DERIVED (geometric-mean band centres) instead of asserted, then VALIDATED by containment in Miller's independently-measured 7+-2.
_meta.derivation: ratio = geomean(slow_gamma_lo, slow_gamma_hi) / geomean(theta_lo, theta_hi) = sqrt((25*50)/(4*8)) = sqrt(39.0625) = 6.25; the geometric-mean band centre is the package's own non-tuned method (the same construction the §14 'geometric-mean cell' uses).
_meta.validated_claim: the dimensionless count of slow-gamma sub-cycles nested in one theta cycle (= the theta-gamma working-memory span, Lisman & Jensen 2013) is CONTAINED in Miller's measured 7+-2 = [5,9]. The band edges come from electrophysiology; the 7+-2 bound comes from psychophysics - independent sources that AGREE, so the agreement (not a fit) is the claim.
_meta.falsifiability_note: the containment has teeth: BROAD gamma (30-100 Hz) gives geomean ratio sqrt((30*100)/(4*8)) = sqrt(93.75) = 9.6825, OUTSIDE [5,9] -> FAIL. The check therefore SELECTS the biologically-correct theta-coupled SLOW gamma (Colgin 2009); it does not assume it.
_meta.open_O: the ABSOLUTE theta and gamma frequencies in Hz: they depend on the absolute inhibitory time-constant tau_inh (an external calibration), so only the dimensionless ratio is pinned (matches the §03 chapter's [O]).
_meta.no_tuning_note: no number here is chosen to hit 7. The four band edges are canonical/measured inputs; the ratio is derived; the validation is containment in an independent bound. If the edges had been the broad gamma band, the gate would FAIL - which is the point.
_meta.payload_sha256_note: sha256 over json.dumps(measured, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':')) - the gate asserts this on load; any silent edit fails it.

theta_band_hz.ref: canonical human theta band (standard clinical EEG taxonomy; oscillation-class review Buzsaki & Draguhn 2004, Science 304:1926-1929)
theta_band_hz.note: theta 4-8 Hz is the standard clinical human theta range used for the theta-gamma code (Lisman & Jensen 2013).

slow_gamma_band_hz.ref: Colgin LL, Denninger T, Fyhn M, Hafting T, Bonnevie T, Jensen O, Moser MB, Moser EI (2009) Nature 462(7271):353-357
slow_gamma_band_hz.note: the SLOW gamma component (25-50 Hz) is the band that couples to theta (CA3->CA1 storage pathway); fast gamma (80-140 Hz) couples to medial entorhinal cortex instead. The theta-NESTED gamma is therefore the slow band.

miller_capacity_items.ref: Miller GA (1956) Psychol Rev 63(2):81-97, 'The magical number seven, plus or minus two'
miller_capacity_items.note: human immediate-memory / channel-capacity span 7+-2 = [5,9]; an INDEPENDENT psychophysical measurement (no EEG), used here only as the containment bound.

mechanism_ref.ref: Lisman JE, Jensen O (2013) Neuron 77(6):1002-1016, 'The Theta-Gamma Neural Code'
mechanism_ref.note: the number of gamma sub-cycles nested in one theta cycle = f_gamma/f_theta = the working-memory span. This identity makes the dimensionless ratio the load-bearing quantity, not the absolute Hz.
